pictures.scene: Emanuel de Witte, Interior of the Oude Kerk in Amsterdam during a Sermon — a tall whitewashed Gothic church of clustered columns and pointed arches where a preacher in black leans out of a pulpit set against a pillar, men in black hats sit behind a long panelled screen, a gilded organ and a brass chandelier hang at the right, and a woman, a man, two children and a brown and white dog stand on the sunlit stone floor in front, in those days the crowd once again became very large, and they had nothing to eat, jesus called the disciples to him and said, i have compassion for this crowd, because they have already been with me three days and have nothing to eat

pictures.scene: Edvard Petersen, Emigrants on the Quay — weary families crowded onto a harbour quay beneath the dark hull of a steamer and the rigging of a sailing ship, a small girl in a black hat and apron holding an orange, her mother in a black shawl with a red capped toddler on her lap, old women in white caps resting on bundles, and men pushing a handcart of trunks under a grey sky, if i send them home hungry, they will faint along the way, for some of them have come a great distance, his disciples replied, where in this desolate place could anyone find enough bread to feed all these people

pictures.scene: Fritz von Uhde, Come Lord Jesus Be Our Guest — Christ in a worn blue robe and bare feet standing with a faint halo inside a dim peasant cottage, the labourer of the house in a blue smock and clogs ushering Him in with both hands towards the round table where a woman and three children wait beside white plates, spoons and a single loaf under whitewashed walls and dark beams, how many loaves do you have, jesus asked, seven, they replied, and he instructed the crowd to sit down on the ground, then he took the seven loaves, gave thanks and broke them, and gave them to his disciples to set before the people, and they distributed them to the crowd
pictures.name: pd_uhde_the_mealtime_prayer

pictures.scene: Joachim Beuckelaer, The Vegetable Market — a market woman in a white shift with rolled sleeves and a red bodice reaching out across wide wicker baskets heaped with pears, apples, plums, walnuts, cherries and grapes, with cabbages and artichokes piled at her feet under the timbers of a market shed, they also had a few small fish, and jesus blessed them and ordered that these be set before them as well, the people ate and were satisfied, and the disciples picked up seven basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over

pictures.scene: Jan Brueghel, The Sermon on the Mount — Christ in white preaching with one hand raised at the centre of an enormous crowd seated and standing on a wooded slope, hundreds of listeners in black hats, white caps and red, yellow and blue dress pressed together, a woman in gold satin with a small dog in the foreground, and tall green trees filling the top of the picture, and about four thousand men were present, as soon as jesus had dismissed the crowd, he got into the boat with his disciples and went to the district of dalmanutha

pictures.scene: Edouard Brandon, Scene in a Synagogue — a man in a pale prayer shawl carrying a crowned Torah scroll up carpeted steps while elders in broad black hats and striped shawls crowd behind him, a boy in a long white robe holds up two lit candles, and a congregation watches over a carved wooden screen beneath dark piers, then the pharisees came and began to argue with jesus, testing him by demanding from him a sign from heaven, jesus sighed deeply in his spirit and said, why does this generation demand a sign, truly i tell you, no sign will be given to this generation

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Christ in the Storm on the Sea of Galilee — a small fishing boat pitched almost upright on a breaking wave with its mast and torn sail filling the upper half against a black storm sky, one man clinging to the rigging, another bent over the side, the disciples clutching the rail and one another, and Christ seated calm in the stern, and he left them, got back into the boat, and crossed to the other side, now the disciples had forgotten to take bread, except for one loaf they had with them in the boat

pictures.scene: Jan Steen, As the Old Sing So Pipe the Young — a crowded merry household where a grandmother in a black hood reads from a song sheet, a laughing man in a broad black hat holds out a long clay pipe to a child, a woman nurses a swaddled infant, wine is poured from a pewter jug into a glass, and oysters and fruit lie on a carpet covered table above a brown and white spaniel, watch out, he cautioned them, beware of the leaven of the pharisees and of herod, so they began to discuss with one another the fact that they had no bread

pictures.scene: Albrecht Durer, Christ among the Doctors — the boy Christ in a green robe counting out His argument on His fingers, ringed close by the gnarled hands and lined faces of the doctors, one old man shouting into His ear and white bearded elders pressing in with heavy clasped books, aware of their conversation, jesus asked them, why are you debating about having no bread, do you still not see or understand, do you have such hard hearts, having eyes, do you not see, and having ears, do you not hear, and do you not remember

pictures.scene: Jean-Francois Millet, Woman Baking Bread — a peasant woman in a yellow headscarf, blue bodice and red sash seen from behind as she slides a pale loaf on a long wooden peel into the glowing mouth of a brick oven in a dark beamed bakehouse, when i broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many basketfuls of broken pieces did you collect, twelve, they answered, and when i broke the seven loaves for the four thousand, how many basketfuls of broken pieces did you collect, seven, they said

pictures.scene: John Everett Millais, The Blind Girl — a blind girl in a brown cloak with a concertina on her lap and a placard asking pity for the blind at her neck, her eyes closed and her face lifted to the sun, her small sister in blue leaning on her shoulder and looking back at a double rainbow over a green meadow with cattle and a village, then he asked them, do you still not understand, when they arrived at bethsaida, some people brought a blind man and begged jesus to touch him

pictures.scene: El Greco, Christ Healing the Blind — Christ in rose and blue stepping forward to take a man by the arm on a tiled pavement, a group kneeling at the right where an old man bends close to peer into another man's eyes, and tall Renaissance arcades receding behind them, so he took the blind man by the hand and led him out of the village, then he spit on the man's eyes and placed his hands on him, can you see anything, he asked, the man looked up and said, i can see the people, but they look like trees walking around

pictures.scene: Anna Ancher, Sunshine in the Blind Woman's Room — an old woman in a black hood and teal sleeves standing beside a scrubbed table while the sun throws bright squares of window light across the wall next to her, a yellow glass jar and small things resting on the sill and a wooden chair in shadow, once again jesus placed his hands on the man's eyes, and when he opened them his sight was restored, and he could see everything clearly, jesus sent him home and said, do not go back into the village

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Parable of the Rich Fool — an old man in a fur trimmed cloak and black cap with spectacles on his nose holding a coin up to the flame of a single candle, hemmed in by ledgers, bundled papers, money bags, scales and a scatter of gold coins across the table, for whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for my sake and for the gospel will save it, what does it profit a man to gain the whole world, yet forfeit his soul

pictures.scene: Fra Angelico, Christ in Glory — Christ enthroned in a deep blue mandorla ringed with blue cherub heads and red seraphim with His right hand raised in blessing, gold rays filling the whole ground, haloed saints and angels in blue, rose and gold standing in prayer at either side and an angel below holding up a tall cross, or what can a man give in exchange for his soul, if anyone is ashamed of me and my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the son of man will also be ashamed of him when he comes in his father's glory with the holy angels

lines.text: In those days the crowd once again became very large, and they had nothing to eat. Jesus called the disciples to Him and said,
I have compassion for this crowd, because they have already been with Me three days and have nothing to eat.
If I send them home hungry, they will faint along the way. For some of them have come a great distance.
His disciples replied, Where in this desolate place could anyone find enough bread to feed all these people?
How many loaves do you have? Jesus asked. Seven, they replied.

And He instructed the crowd to sit down on the ground. Then He took the seven loaves, gave thanks and broke them, and gave them to His disciples to set before the people. And they distributed them to the crowd.
They also had a few small fish, and Jesus blessed them and ordered that these be set before them as well.
The people ate and were satisfied, and the disciples picked up seven basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over.
And about four thousand men were present. As soon as Jesus had dismissed the crowd,
He got into the boat with His disciples and went to the district of Dalmanutha.
Then the Pharisees came and began to argue with Jesus, testing Him by demanding from Him a sign from heaven.
Jesus sighed deeply in His spirit and said, Why does this generation demand a sign? Truly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation.
And He left them, got back into the boat, and crossed to the other side.
Now the disciples had forgotten to take bread, except for one loaf they had with them in the boat.
Watch out! He cautioned them. Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of Herod.
So they began to discuss with one another the fact that they had no bread.
Aware of their conversation, Jesus asked them, Why are you debating about having no bread? Do you still not see or understand? Do you have such hard hearts?
Having eyes, do you not see? And having ears, do you not hear? And do you not remember?
When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many basketfuls of broken pieces did you collect? Twelve, they answered.
And when I broke the seven loaves for the four thousand, how many basketfuls of broken pieces did you collect? Seven, they said.
Then He asked them, Do you still not understand?
When they arrived at Bethsaida, some people brought a blind man and begged Jesus to touch him.
So He took the blind man by the hand and led him out of the village. Then He spit on the man's eyes and placed His hands on him. Can you see anything? He asked.
The man looked up and said, I can see the people, but they look like trees walking around.
Once again Jesus placed His hands on the man's eyes, and when he opened them his sight was restored, and he could see everything clearly.
Jesus sent him home and said, Do not go back into the village.
Then Jesus and His disciples went on to the villages around Caesarea Philippi. On the way, He questioned His disciples: Who do people say I am?
They replied, Some say John the Baptist; others say Elijah; and still others, one of the prophets.
But what about you? Jesus asked. Who do you say I am? Peter answered, You are the Christ.
And Jesus warned them not to tell anyone about Him.
Then He began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and that He must be killed and after three days rise again.
He spoke this message quite frankly, and Peter took Him aside and began to rebuke Him.
But Jesus, turning and looking at His disciples, rebuked Peter and said, Get behind Me, Satan! For you do not have in mind the things of God, but the things of men.
Then Jesus called the crowd to Him along with His disciples, and He told them, If anyone wants to come after Me, he must deny himself and take up his cross and follow Me.
For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for My sake and for the gospel will save it.
What does it profit a man to gain the whole world, yet forfeit his soul?
Or what can a man give in exchange for his soul?
If anyone is ashamed of Me and My words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when He comes in His Father's glory with the holy angels.
